extracted.intended_audience: registrants (issuers), accountants, auditors, and securities lawyers preparing SEC filings for blind-pool and other real estate acquisitions
extracted.subtask_short: SEC reporting for blind-pool real estate
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on applying Regulation S-X significance tests and related SEC reporting and disclosure requirements (S-X Rule 3-14, Rule 3-05, Rule 11-01, Industry Guide 5, SAB Topic 1.I) for blind-pool real estate offerings and mortgage-secured transactions. Covers timing of tests, modified denominators/numerators, filing undertakings (sticker supplements, post-effective amendments, Form 8-K), and thresholds for required financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance threshold requiring S-X Rule 3-14/3-05 financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If significance exceeds 20% for an acquisition (including acquisitions of a group of related businesses), financial statements must be filed for the periods indicated by S-X Rule 3-14 (or Rule 3-05). [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(1)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 20% significance threshold is the filing trigger for audited financial statements under Rule 3-14 (real estate operations) or Rule 3-05 (other businesses). Apply the applicable significance test (investment, asset, or income where relevant) to determine whether the threshold is exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of investment test under S-X Rule 3-14 (real estate acquisitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine significance using the investment test for S-X Rule 3-14 acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For real estate operations, the investment test generally uses 'Investments in and advances to the acquired business (purchase price)' as the numerator and the registrant’s AWMV (or modified denominator if AWMV not available) as the denominator. For blind-pool offerings the test may be modified per S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of investment and asset tests under S-X Rule 3-05
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine significance using investment and asset tests for S-X Rule 3-05 acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 3-05 uses both the investment test and the asset test; however, under Rule 3-05 the numerator is not subject to the blind-pool modifications allowed for S-X Rule 3-14 (i.e., 'Numerator – no modifications allowed [S-X Rule 3-05(b)(2)]').

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test exclusion for blind pool offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: The income test does not apply to blind pool offerings, and the investment test and asset test are not applied in the same way they are applied in other situations. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating blind pool offerings, do not use the income test; instead follow the specific adapted tests and requirements described for blind pools in S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4) and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified investment test when AWMV not available (during distribution period)
rubrics_metrics.description: For blind pool real estate offerings where AWMV is not available, apply an adapted investment test: numerator = Investments in and advances to the acquired business + Any assumed debt secured by the real properties; denominator = Registrant’s consolidated total assets as of the acquisition date + Proceeds to be raised in the registered offering over the next 12 months. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4)(i)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registrant calculates the numerator consistent with other acquisitions of real estate operations (see section 8.3.10). When using consolidated total assets as the denominator, include expected net proceeds to be raised in the next 12 months to avoid deeming virtually all early acquisitions significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator modification: include expected offering proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: When the investment test is based on consolidated total assets in a blind pool offering, S-X Rule 11-01 requires the registrant to include the proceeds (net of commissions) in good faith expected to be raised in the registered offering over the next 12 months. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4)(i)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate proceeds (net of commissions) to include in the denominator; see guidance on estimating offering proceeds (pace of fundraising, sponsor experience, similar offerings). This accommodation prevents early acquisitions from being automatically significant for blind pools with no assets yet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerator modification: include assumed debt when using total assets denominator (S-X Rule 3-14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator - include any assumed debt secured by the real properties if using total assets for denominator [S-X Rule 3-14(b)(2)(ii)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using total assets as the denominator for S-X Rule 3-14 significance calculations, incorporate assumed debt secured by the real properties into the numerator (investments and advances) to reflect transaction economics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerator not modifiable under S-X Rule 3-05 during blind pool distribution period
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator – no modifications allowed [S-X Rule 3-05(b)(2)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For acquisitions in the scope of S-X Rule 3-05 during a blind pool distribution period, do not apply the blind-pool numerator accommodations — use the standard numerator definitions for investment/asset tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of performing significance tests (during vs after distribution period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different adapted tests and denominator/numerator treatments apply depending on whether the acquisition occurs during the distribution period or after the distribution period of a blind pool offering. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During distribution period: include expected offering proceeds in denominator and apply adapted numerators per rule. After distribution period: different adapted tests apply until first annual report is filed; after first Form 10-K, revert to normal significance calculations described in section 8.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of acquired business assets from denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining significance, the denominator in each significance test excludes assets of the acquired business from the registrant’s consolidated financial information. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the acquired business’s assets in the denominator when computing significance — i.e., exclude the assets of the acquired business from the registrant’s consolidated total assets for the test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating offering proceeds for denominator inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: In estimating the offering proceeds, the SEC staff has stated the registrant should consider the pace of fundraising as of the measurement date, the sponsor or dealer-manager's prior public fundraising experience, and offerings by similar entities. [FRM 2325.3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observable/credible fundraising metrics as of the measurement date; document assumptions (pace, sponsor track record, peer offerings) used to estimate proceeds expected to be raised over next 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sticker supplement filing obligation during distribution period (Industry Guide 5 Item 20.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sticker supplement is filed whenever a reasonable probability exists that a property will be acquired. The supplement must describe each significant real estate operation that was not identified in the prospectus and include information required for significant properties in Items 14 and 15 of Form S-11. [Industry Guide 5 Item 20.D, FRM 2325.2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File sticker supplements to disclose newly probable significant property acquisitions identified during distribution; include the detailed narrative and property-specific items required by Form S-11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-effective amendment consolidation and frequency (Industry Guide 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-effective amendment must be filed at least once every three months to consolidate all sticker supplements and must include or incorporate by reference audited financial statements under S-X Rule 3-14 for all acquired significant real estate operations that have been filed or should have been filed on Form 8-K. Pro forma information also is required. [FRM 2325.2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidate sticker supplements quarterly into a post-effective amendment; ensure required S-X 3-14 audited financial statements and pro forma disclosures are included or incorporated by reference as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-effective amendment for a fundamental change must include financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-effective amendment filed as a result of a fundamental change (as required by S-K Item 512(a)) must include financial statements for all significant acquisitions, including financial statements not yet filed during the 71-day extension period. [FRM 2325.2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a fundamental change triggers a post-effective amendment, include all required audited financial statements for significant acquisitions even if they otherwise would have been eligible for a 71-day Form 8-K extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing requirement during distribution period for consummated significant acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: During the distribution period of a blind pool offering, a Form 8-K that includes S-X Rule 3-14 financial statements and the related pro forma information must be filed in a timely manner to report all real estate acquisitions that exceed the 20% significance level once the acquisition has been consummated. [FRM 2325.4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File Form 8-K promptly after consummation of an acquisition that crosses the 20% threshold, including required S-X 3-14 audited financial statements and pro forma information; if audited financial statements already filed in a sticker/post-effective and are 'substantially the same', updated financials may not be required (see Question 4.3.40 guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: 71-day Form 8-K extension does not apply to post-effective amendment consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: The 71-day extension period permitted under Form 8-K, Item 9.01 to file the financial statements for an acquired real estate operation and related pro forma information does not apply to filing post-effective amendments required under Item 20.D of Industry Guide 5 (i.e. every three months). [C&DI Exch Act Form 8-K §229.01]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While Form 8-K Item 9.01 provides a 71-day extension for certain 8-K financial statement filings, that extension does not excuse the timeliness of post-effective amendments consolidating sticker supplements under Industry Guide 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales during the 71-day extension period
rubrics_metrics.description: If real estate operations are acquired during the offering period and financial statements for the acquired real estate operation have not yet been filed on Form 8-K, the SEC staff has stated a registrant may continue sales activities during the 71-day extension period as long as the post-effective amendments containing the financial statements of the acquired properties are filed when required by Item 20.D of Industry Guide 5. [C&DI Exch Act Form 8-K §229.02]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants need not suspend sales during the 71-day 8-K extension so long as they comply with Industry Guide 5 timing for sticker/post-effective filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-effective amendments consolidating sticker supplements may not require updated financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-effective amendments that consolidate supplements are not considered new filings for purposes of updating the financial statements if they are filed by entities under Item 20.D of Industry Guide 5 solely to provide the financial statements of acquired businesses. [FRM 2325.2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consolidating sticker supplements for the narrow purpose of furnishing acquired-business financials, registrants may rely on the previously filed financial statements without updating to current S-X Rule 3-12 age requirements at time of consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-distribution period adapted investment test until first annual report
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4) requires a registrant to determine significance using the adapted investment test until it files its first annual report after the distribution period ends. After the distribution period has ended, the registrant determines significance using total assets as of the acquisition date, excluding assets of the acquired business, until it files its next Form 10-K. After that next Form 10-K is filed, the registrant determines significance in the normal manner. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After distribution, continue to apply adapted rules (denominator excluding acquired assets, adapted numerator) until the first Form 10-K; thereafter, revert to standard S-X significance calculations for real estate acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC staff position on individually insignificant properties (post-distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff has not objected to the view that the undertaking to provide audited financial statements is not applicable to individually insignificant properties. Therefore, S-X Rule 3-14 financial statements may be omitted for individually insignificant properties. This position is consistent with Form 8-K guidance, which does not require a registrant to aggregate individually insignificant acquisitions. [FRM 2325.5, CFDG Topic 6]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants may omit S-X 3-14 audited statements for individually insignificant properties; evaluate whether aggregation is required only when filing registration/proxy statements or when other rules require aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Guide 5 contrasting disclosure obligation (10% threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry Guide 5 states that a Form 8-K containing the financial statements be filed for 'each commitment (i.e. the signing of a binding purchase agreement) made after the end of the distribution period involving the use of 10% or more (on a cumulative basis) of the net proceeds of the offering'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff indicated the Item 20.D post-distribution period 10% measure and Form 8-K trigger do not benefit investors and add complexity; reconcile Industry Guide 5 positions with staff guidance and applicable filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation requirement for registration/proxy statements filed after distribution but before first Form 10-K
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant were to file a registration or proxy statement after the distribution period but before the first Form 10-K, it would be required to aggregate individually insignificant acquisitions consistent with the requirements for any other registration statement. [Question 8.5.130 / Question 2.3.190]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration/proxy statements demand aggregation of individually insignificant acquisitions for disclosure; do not rely on the post-distribution individually-insignificant exception when preparing registration/proxy filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different adapted tests for non-real-estate blind pool offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: The adapted significance test for blind pool real estate offerings is not the same for other blind pool offerings (i.e., non-real estate) during the distribution period. Although the denominator (if using total assets) is calculated in the same manner, the numerator is not. [Question 8.5.140]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-real-estate blind pool offerings in the scope of S-X Rule 3-05, apply the specific asset/investment test numerators and do not assume S-X 3-14 accommodations apply; consult S-X Rule 3-05 guidance for numerators.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-14 definition of 'real estate operation' and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'real estate operation' means a business that generates substantially all of its revenues through the leasing of real property. The acquisition of a real estate operation encompasses the acquisition of an interest in a real estate operation accounted for by the equity method or, in lieu of the equity method, the fair value option. [S-X Rule 3-14(a)(2)(i)-(ii)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether an acquired asset or interest qualifies as a 'real estate operation' (leasing revenue focus) and whether equity-method interests fall within S-X Rule 3-14 scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAB Topic 1.I: when properties securing mortgage loans require financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: SAB Topic 1.I indicates that operating properties underlying mortgage loans should be included as required by Rule 3-14 when the mortgage has the economic substance of an investment in real estate or a joint venture rather than a loan; characteristics to consider are identified in ADC Arrangements subsection of ASC 310-10. Financial presentation required when loans represent significant concentration. [SAB Topic 1.I]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess characteristics (participation in expected residual profit, extent of lender funding, borrower equity, contractual payment structure) to determine whether the transaction is economically an investment; if so, include operating-property financial statements per Rule 3-14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators for loan-versus-investment accounting (FASB ASC references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain characteristics of a lending arrangement indicate the 'lender' has the same risks and potential rewards as an owner or joint venturer; consider ADC Arrangements Subsection of ASC 310-10 and ASC 815-15 (embedded derivatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the embedded expected residual profit component need not be bifurcated as a derivative, follow the ADC guidance and include disclosures/financials for ADC-like mortgage loans. Evaluate borrower’s initial investment per ASC 360-20-40-18 and continuing investment per ASC 360-20-40-19 when assessing loan accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: When loans exceed 20% of expected proceeds require property financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amount of a loan exceeds 20% of the amount in good faith expected to be raised in the offering, disclosures would be expected to consist of financial statements for the underlying operating properties for the periods contemplated by Rule 3-14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If single or related loans to a person/group aggregate >20% of expected proceeds, include underlying-property financial statements; this addresses concentration risk and aligns with Rule 3-13/Rule 408 considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1-02(w) substitution and significance computation for mortgage loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 1-02(w) of Regulation S-X includes the conditions used in determining whether an acquisition is significant. The separate financial statements of an individual property should be provided when a property would meet the requirements for a significant subsidiary under this rule using the amount of the 'loan' as a substitute for the 'investment in the subsidiary' in computing the specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute Rule 1-02(w) tests substituting loan amount for investment to determine whether separate audited financial statements of the property are required; combined financials may be omitted if combined conditions do not exceed 20% in aggregate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment under 1934 Act filings for significant mortgage-secured investments
rubrics_metrics.description: For filings under the 1934 Act, the staff believes that filings should include the same financial and other information relating to properties underlying any loans which are significant as discussed, except that the 20% disclosure threshold should be measured using total assets. [Interpretive Response]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing 1934 Act filings (e.g., Form 10-K, Form 8-K where applicable), measure the 20% significance threshold using total assets to determine whether property financials for mortgage-secured investments are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment-type arrangements: 10% threshold for audited financial statements (Securities Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate audited financial statements should be provided for any investment-type arrangement that constitutes 10% or more of the greater of (i) the amount of minimum proceeds or (ii) the total assets of the registrant, including the amount of proceeds raised, as of the date the filing is required to be made. Narrative information required by items 14 and 15 of Form S-11 should also be included. [Interpretive Response]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an investment-type arrangement equals or exceeds the 10% metric, provide separate audited financials and narrative; document the computation base (minimum proceeds vs total assets including proceeds) and the filing date used for measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment-type arrangements below 10% but aggregated >20%: narrative disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific financial information need be presented for investment-type arrangements that amount to less than 10%. However, where such arrangements aggregate more than 20%, a narrative description of the general character of the properties and arrangements should be included that gives an investor an understanding of the risks and rewards associated with these arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For <10% individual arrangements that aggregate >20%, include descriptive disclosure (terms, participation in residual profits, property types/locations) to inform investors of concentration and risk characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K triggered by acquisition of investment-type arrangement: separate audited financial statements required at 10%
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are reminded that in filings on Form 8-K that are triggered in connection with an acquisition of an investment-type arrangement, separate audited financial statements are required for any such arrangement that individually constitutes 10% or more. [Footnote note]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an acquisition of an investment-type arrangement triggers Form 8-K, check whether the 10% individual threshold is met; if so, include separate audited financial statements in the 8-K filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping of which S-X rules may require property financial information across filing types
rubrics_metrics.description: SAB Topic 1.I contemplates S-X Rule 3-09, S-X Rule 3-13, and S-X Rule 3-14 (and related rules such as Rule 4-08(g) and Rule 408) which may require financial information of underlying properties securing mortgage loans depending on filing type (Form 8-K, registration statement, Form 10-K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the document's summary table to determine which rule(s) apply to the specific filing type: Rule 3-09/4-08(g), Rule 3-13/Rule 408, and Rule 3-14 have differing applicability to Form 8-Ks, registration statements, and Form 10-Ks — confirm rule applicability before preparing filings.
